Experiencing this issue using the 4.5 version flatpak (v4.5.stable.flathub [876b29033]) on Bazzite 42, Wayland, Nvidia GPU. I was not experiencing this issue on 4.4. 

Right after opening the editor, there are no issues but after a few minutes of working it always freezes after hovering over a tooltip or opening a dropdown menu. I've had it happen on any tooltip whether in project/editor settings, the gltf import settings window, animation tree, etc. 

When it freezes it hangs indefinitely forcing me to pkill it

Also expriencing this issue with the v4.5.stable.official [876b29033] binary downloaded from godotengine.org

I did some more testing and realized I don't know enough about godot or wayland to figure out the cause but here are some notes:

* The solution in #110333 of running godot in single window mode (--single-window) actually worked and stopped these freezes altogether, but I'm not sure that its the same issue.
* Enabling 'Prefer Wayland ' stops the editor from freezing when interatcting with color picker, but does not stop crashing from other popups/tooltip sources.
* I think its related to tooltips or dropdown menus with lots of items. If I open a new clean project in 4.5 and go to the input map and add a new event, moving the mouse through the list of all possible input events will eventually cause the freeze.
* In a fresh project, importing an fbx with multiple animations, and then creating an animation tree and right clicking to open the add animation tooltip that lists all the available anims will also lead to the freeze
* I tried this with the flatpak, the official linux binary, and with 4.6 dev build and still got the same issue.

I attached a debugger to a `dev` build and it seems that it gets stuck in this line:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/0f3e975aac52e87b76a5a0913100fc6341c892a2/drivers/vulkan/rendering_device_driver_vulkan.cpp#L2549

I changed the `timeout` parameter to 1 second (in nanoseconds) in the function [`vKWaitForFences()`](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/man/html/vkWaitForFences.html) and ran the editor with the flags `--gpu-validation` and `--gpu-abort`. Now when the problem happens I get the following error:

```text
ERROR: Condition "err != VK_SUCCESS" is true. Returning: FAILED
   at: fence_wait (drivers/vulkan/rendering_device_driver_vulkan.cpp:2550)
ERROR: VALIDATION - Message Id Number: -1254218959 | Message Id Name: VUID-vkResetCommandPool-commandPool-00040
        vkResetCommandPool(): (VkCommandBuffer 0x556d88745970) is in use.
The Vulkan spec states: All VkCommandBuffer objects allocated from commandPool must not be in the pending state (https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/cmdbuffers.html#VUID-vkResetCommandPool-commandPool-00040)
        Objects - 2
                Object[0] - VK_OBJECT_TYPE_COMMAND_BUFFER, Handle 93928929122672
                Object[1] - VK_OBJECT_TYPE_COMMAND_POOL, Handle 45079976738857
   at: _debug_messenger_callback (drivers/vulkan/rendering_context_driver_vulkan.cpp:642)
ERROR: Crashing, because abort on GPU errors is enabled.
   at: _debug_messenger_callback (drivers/vulkan/rendering_context_driver_vulkan.cpp:643)
``` 

I think the validation message is just a side effect of the `vkWaitForFences()` function timing out and it isn’t the core issue.

Hopefully someone with more knowledge about all this can find out the problem 😅

I tested a bunch of versions down to v4.0.alpha1.official [31a7ddbf8] following these steps to trigger the freeze: * Open the project settings and go to the `Input Map` tab * Enable `Show built-in actions` * Open the dialog to add an input event to an action (click the `+` icon next to an input action) * Un-fold the `Keyboard keys` section and start scrolling up and down This will trigger the freeze randomly. I tried to build a dev build from that commit to see if it freezes in the same function but I wasn't able because I get a lot of errors and I'm not 100% how to fix those 😅 I did launch the official build with a debugger and, although I didn't have debug symbols, the backtrace looked similar to the one I was getting with other builds. I've seen similar issues opened with a similar behavior and I think they are probably all the same: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/100265 (this one is on Windows) https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/110783 https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/110620 https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/110333 etc. Update: I tried to trigger the freeze on X11 and I wasn't able to. I'm not sure if the issue is not present there or if it takes more time to appear. At this point I'm more inclined to think that the issue is in the nvidia driver side when running on Wayland. - Have the main editor window + the script window floating + a color picker on a colorrect open (which equals 3 floating windows)

-  Editor freezes completely after a few seconds (about 10 - 20)

**PopOS Scenario 1:**

-  Godot Editor Settings -> the checkbox "prefer wayland" = true

-  SAME as above with CachyOS -> full freeze

**PopOS Scenario 2:**

- Godot Editor Settings -> the checkbox "prefer wayland" = false

- Have the main editor window + the script window floating + a color picker on a colorrect open (which equals 3 floating windows)

- Editor does not freeze but becomes extremely stuttery and laggy until I close one of the floating windows

Debian 13, KDE Plasma 6.5.3, Wayland, Nvidia GTX 1650 with driver 580.82.07, has been happening since Godot 4.5+, currently on `master` branch with the latest build. I thought it was just my fork where I modified some stuff, but nope.

Same issue here, and I could reproduce the input built-in actions scenario immediately, but it happens in other instances that were previously mentioned, such as pop-ups, hover tooltips, dropdowns, and input fields.

The editor does NOT crash, it just freezes indefinitely, both the GUI and terminal output if running with --verbose.


The thing that confused me most is that Godot doesn't show any logging about this when running from the terminal, logging just stops when this freeze happens. My first reaction was that maybe the editor was coredumping, but as I didn't find any dumps, it prompted me to investigate using gdb.

I ran `gdb -p {godot pid} -batch -ex "thread apply all bt" -ex "info threads" -ex "call (void)fflush(stdout)"` in order to see backtraces for all the threads used by the project while the engine was frozen, and to me it also seems like a driver issue.
